assertions.name: assertion_api_is_not_a_central_lever
assertions.source: 461 of 26980 non-integral float leaves sit under .assertions[] (1.71 %). Stated as a predicate (under 5 %) so the witness summary reports a pass for a measured negative rather than FAILURES.

description: Bean qou-oots. Asks whether the raw-float64 backlog (33,702 fields / 1015 witnesses after the 2026-09-06 ratchet) is reachable by a CENTRAL fix, and answers NO with the measurements. Records that the obvious candidate -- WitnessBuilder.add_assertion, whose `expected`/`computed` are the most WIDESPREAD dirty leaf names -- is a false lead twice over: integral floats are excluded from the count and were inflating that ranking ~3x (assertions are 1.6 % of non-integral leaves), and the `_tolerance_literal` mechanism cannot be generalised to `expected` because the significant-digit bimodality that justifies its cut does not exist there. Reports where the work actually is, by producer bucket, so a campaign has a starting point.

population.note: Integral floats are EXCLUDED, matching the audit's own `_count(integral_is_exact=True)`. Counting them measures a different population and inflates every name ranking.

central_fix_candidates.verdict: The assertion API is under 2 % of the backlog, NOT a lever. Solver output is ~10 % and is float64 because scipy and Clarabel are -- not a serialization slip, and not fixed by carrying mpf to the boundary.

why_tolerance_mechanism_does_not_general.tolerance_has_empty_bin_at_6: per _tolerance_literal's docstring, which is what makes its cut a cluster boundary rather than a tuned knob
why_tolerance_mechanism_does_not_general.conclusion: Extending _tolerance_literal to `expected` would require choosing a threshold with no empirical boundary -- exactly what that docstring declines to do. The mechanism is correct where it is and must not be generalised on the analogy alone.

where_the_work_is.reading: B is where the mass is and is the more tractable half: the arithmetic is already mpmath and only the write is missing, so routing it through `fmt` is mechanical. It is a CANDIDATE class, not a guaranteed one -- `import mpmath` does not establish that the DIRTY LEAF was computed in mpf, so confirm per producer. A is expensive under any reading: the computation itself is f64, so changing it moves recorded numbers. 'unresolved producer' is this script's resolver, not necessarily a defect class.
where_the_work_is.predicate_correction: The first run of this audit had B and C swapped (C read 463 files / 15,189 fields against a true 81 / 2,054) because binds_fmt asked `"_precision import" in src`, a substring that `from _precision import set_compute_dps` satisfies without binding fmt. 377 producers were misfiled and the audit's own recommendation about where to start was inverted. Now an AST walk -- see binds_fmt.

q0AnchorReason: structural audit of the committed witness corpus and producer sources (float-leaf counts, AST import buckets); computes no q-dependent quantity and never reads q0
